title: From SDET to AI quality engineer
objectives: Distinguish testing with AI from testing AI
Map existing SDET skills to probabilistic systems
Identify the evidence needed to release an AI feature
relevance: You already understand contracts, coverage, regression, and release risk. AI extends these skills to systems where valid answers can vary between runs.

sections.title: Two tracks, one engineering mindset
paragraphs: Track A uses AI to improve software testing: generating API test candidates, classifying CI failures, or proposing missing edge cases. The generated artifacts still need review and deterministic execution.

Track B tests the AI application itself: whether a chatbot stays grounded, whether retrieval finds the right document, and whether an agent calls an authorized tool. Treat its output as evidence to evaluate, not a trustworthy oracle.

sections.title: Deterministic contracts, probabilistic behavior
paragraphs: A REST endpoint may promise an exact status code and schema. A chatbot can express the same correct answer in many ways. Separate hard invariants (valid JSON, no forbidden tool, citation points to supplied evidence) from quality rubrics (helpfulness, completeness, groundedness).

Freeze representative test inputs and application versions. Run repeated samples when variation matters. Record outputs, scores, cost, latency, and failure categories. One passing response is not proof of reliability.

sections.title: Your learning path
paragraphs: Build Python, data, SQL, and statistical foundations before abstractions. Then learn embeddings and retrieval before RAG frameworks; tool calling before agents; evaluation before release.

An AI engineer assembles useful model-powered systems. An ML engineer develops model training and serving pipelines. A data scientist investigates data and experiments. An AI quality engineer designs evidence and controls across those systems. Roles overlap; judge work by its purpose.

mistake: Using exact text equality for every LLM response rejects good paraphrases and misses groundedness failures.
takeaway: Preserve deterministic invariants and measure uncertain behavior across a representative dataset.

exercise.explanation: Building an AI helper belongs to AI engineering; evaluating its output belongs to testing AI; training its learned classifier belongs to ML engineering.

title: A reproducible engineering workspace
objectives: Isolate dependencies in a virtual environment
Keep secrets out of browser applications
relevance: A reproducible lab turns a notebook experiment into a testable CI artifact that colleagues can run.

sections.title: An environment is part of the program
paragraphs: Use a project-specific virtual environment. Select its interpreter in VS Code. Keep dependency declarations in the repository and record the Python version in your README. A package imported from your global machine can hide a missing dependency.

A notebook is useful for inspecting data and plots. Move durable logic into importable modules with tests. Git should track source and small synthetic datasets, not virtual environments or secret files.
sections.code:
python -m venv .venv
# Linux / macOS
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install pytest
python -m pytest

sections.title: Static safe mode and local labs
paragraphs: The course executes educational Python and SQL in your browser. It has no provider key and no model API requirement. Optional local labs use a Python process on your machine.

A browser bundle is downloadable by every visitor. An environment variable prefixed for Vite client use is still public after bundling. Keep provider credentials exclusively in local processes or a properly authenticated server.
sections.code:
import os
api_key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")
# Never print api_key or commit a populated .env file.

sections.title: Engineering boundaries and independent checks
paragraphs: A notebook is useful for inspecting one experiment, but execution order can hide dependencies: a cell may succeed only because an earlier cell created a variable. Move the analyzer into an importable function and run it from a fresh interpreter. Keep a small notebook as a consumer of that function rather than a second implementation.

Use a virtual environment per project and install from a reviewed manifest. Record Python and package versions with the run artifact; a requirements range alone does not recreate a particular installation. Store a tested lock or freeze after validation. Verify setup with an import smoke test and the analyzer's behavior tests before connecting a provider. A key belongs in the local process environment and must be excluded from Git, browser bundles and progress backups.

mistake: Committing .env or putting a provider key into a VITE_ variable exposes the secret.
takeaway: A clean checkout plus documented setup should reproduce your test results.

exercise.prompt: Put workspace setup in a reproducible order.
exercise.answer: Create virtual environment|Activate interpreter|Install declared dependencies|Run tests
exercise.explanation: Create isolation first, activate it, then install into it and verify the application.

module: Orientation: From SDET To AI Quality Engineer
title: Define an AI release contract
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects define an ai release contract with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Build a small suite with an allowed request, a forbidden request, an unanswerable question, and a valid paraphrase.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An AI feature is a system of deterministic boundaries around probabilistic inference. A useful release contract separates hard constraints from graded usefulness: a tool must never read another tenant’s logs, while a summary may be correct in several phrasings. Model quality cannot compensate for an unauthorized action.

Write a risk register before selecting a framework. Identify who can be harmed, the action scope, evidence sources, uncertainty tolerance, and fallback. An AI quality engineer collaborates on these product decisions rather than merely choosing an evaluator after implementation.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Represent each invariant as an executable predicate and each graded requirement as a documented rubric. Version the dataset, prompt, model, retriever, and policy with the run. Compare matched cases and retain per-case evidence instead of storing only an average.

A project README should distinguish observations on synthetic data from production claims. Define who adjudicates uncertain outputs and how a release can be rolled back. The risk contract becomes acceptance criteria for the learner’s portfolio.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A score of 92% can hide a single severe cross-tenant failure. Segment the report by risk and prohibit aggregation from overriding critical gates. A model refusal is not automatically correct: an authorized, answerable request may have been refused unnecessarily.

Reproduce the request using its exact versions, check the authorization decision, and inspect evidence passed to the model. Determine whether the defect is a broken deterministic boundary or an uncertain response.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Build a small suite with an allowed request, a forbidden request, an unanswerable question, and a valid paraphrase. Record contract compliance separately from usefulness. Show which boundary prevented a forbidden action and which rubric scored the paraphrase.

The release review should include failures, confidence limits, and operating budgets. An SDET’s regression mindset becomes especially valuable when every model upgrade can change behavior without changing application code.

takeaway: Build a small suite with an allowed request, a forbidden request, an unanswerable question, and a valid paraphrase.

exercise.prompt: Design the release contract for a CI-log summarizer that can access two synthetic tenants. Include hard gates, quality evidence, and an outage fallback.
exercise.solution: Authorize tenant access before retrieval, validate the response schema, and reject forbidden tool proposals. Evaluate grounded summaries on a versioned dataset using a calibrated rubric. On outage return a deterministic evidence-only report and retain rollback versions.

quiz.question: A candidate for define an ai release contract meets the happy path but fails the phase's documented counterexample. What is the defensible decision?
options: Hold release, preserve the failing case and fix the responsible boundary
Release because the happy path passed
Delete the failing case to improve the score
quiz.explanation: The failing counterexample disproves the claimed contract. Retain it as regression evidence and rerun the corrected boundary.
